name: Psychobilly wedge

lead: The psychobilly wedge is a hairstyle associated with psychobilly, the punk-meets-rockabilly music scene. Male fans and musicians shaved the sides and back of the head and built the top into a high, wedge-shaped quiff or pompadour, sometimes bleached or dyed.

Its appearance payoff is height and angularity: the tall, swept-up top elongates the head, frames the forehead and emphasises the jawline and cheekbones against the cropped sides. It is a statement style tied to a subculture rather than a conventional cut.

paras: The look is built from a 1950s-style quiff or flat-top left long on top with the back and sides shaved or cropped, then styled upward with strong-hold product, sometimes with colour. Stylists and fans vary the shape, from a sharp wedge to a rounded pompadour.
Little beyond ordinary hair-care concerns: bleaching and repeated heavy styling can dry or damage hair, and the style requires regular upkeep of the shaved sides.

chain: Sides shaved or cropped, top left long
Top is swept up into a tall wedge or quiff
Added height and angular head shape that frames the face
angle.text: The wedge adds vertical height and sharp lines to the top of the head, and the cropped sides expose the jaw and cheekbones. People wear it as a subculture signal as much as a way to alter their silhouette.

lead: The psychobilly wedge is a tall, wedge-shaped quiff or pompadour with shaved or cropped sides, worn by fans and musicians of psychobilly, a genre that blends rockabilly with punk [1]. It descends from 1950s rockabilly hair and was a reaction to the long, greased hair of the British Teddy Boy look; the band the Sharks criticised that look in their 1980 song 'Take a Razor to Your Head' [1].

For appearance, the cut works through height and contrast. The tall top adds vertical length and draws attention to the face, while the cropped sides expose the jaw and ears. In the 1980s scene, people pushed hair as tall as possible and added bright streaks [1]. It is typically paired with the scene's clothing and tattoos, such as studded leather jackets and vintage-themed ink [1].
infobox: Regular trimming of sides, strong-hold styling

paras: Male psychobilly fans and musicians often shaved their heads into a high wedge-shaped pompadour or quiff. Alternatives within the scene included military-style crops and mohawks, and an early version was a 1950s-style quiff or flat-top, often bleached, with the back and sides shaved [1]. Bands such as Mad Sin and Nekromantix are shown in photographs with pompadours and cropped sides [1].

The style grew out of 1950s rockabilly hair and developed in the early 1980s alongside the psychobilly genre, partly as a counter to the Teddy Boy hairstyle [1]. The scene spread internationally and its style combined scooter and skinhead influences, though not every participant adopted them [1].

timeline.event: Rockabilly quiffs and flat-tops establish the base look [1].
The Sharks' 'Take a Razor to Your Head' criticises the Teddy Boy hairstyle [1].
Psychobilly fans push hair as tall as possible, adding colour streaks [1].
